new_findings.text: The packet names §1t4470s0§ but never opens it, so the actual numbers stayed unclaimed. §1t99s0§.as:3048-3051 is `public function §1t4470s0§() : Boolean { return this.§1t4469s0§() && this.§1t4414s0§ >= 48; }` and :3058-3080 is the cycle body, which returns early `if(this.§1t4414s0§ < 48)` and otherwise steps stance -1->Light, Light->Balanced, Balanced->Heavy, Heavy->Light before pushing the value to §1t251s0§. The meter's max is set at :249 as `this.§1t4415s0§ = 8 * 24;` = 192, initialised to 0 at :250. §1t4469s0§ (:3043-3045) is an actionState test, i.e. the gate is 'idle-ish AND meter >= 48'. So the in-combat stance switch costs no Focus and no Chi: it needs the reload meter at 48/192 = 25%. That is the number the recreation should be gating on, and it is the single missing quantity behind the whole CANNOT CHANGE STANCE cluster.

new_findings.text: C2 says the four data XMLs are android-side, so diffing them proves nothing, and that combat tuning parity is NOT established. Here is a bridge that is not circular. Android StatsManager.as:1834 calls `player.initPlayer(0, HP, MAXHP, CHI, MAXCHI, DEFENSE, getBaseReload(), getMinDamage(), getDamageRange(), getBaseSlashLength(), getSlashUsage(), getStat(1000), getStat(1001), getStat(1002), getLevel())` - fifteen named arguments. The web fighter's ctor §1t99s0§.as:188-201 takes exactly fifteen ints and assigns them in exactly that order, including `this.defense = param6` at the DEFENSE slot, which pins the alignment independently. That decodes six obfuscated web fields at once (§1t3257s0§=MAXHP, §1t4413s0§=MAXCHI, §1t4421s0§/§1t4422s0§/§1t4423s0§ = skills 1000/1001/1002, §1t4420s0§=baseSlashLength) and it is what actually rules out an off-by-one in the mastery term.
new_findings.lane_impact: L2 skills-meters + L5 combat-core: an argument-order bridge that names six web fields from android symbols without diffing a file against itself - reusable wherever a web/android pair shares a call signature.

new_findings.text: The ledger's item 3 treats damage and reach as one table scaling together. The web payload says they are mirror images. §1t99s0§.as:3091-3130 is the REACH switch: Light reach is `§1t4420s0§ * 1.4` FLAT with no mastery term (:3094); Balanced reach is `§1t4420s0§ * (1 + 0.2 * §1t4422s0§ * 0.1)` (:3105); Heavy reach is `§1t4420s0§ * (0.5 + 0.4 * §1t4423s0§ * 0.1)` (:3116) with a hard clamp `if(this.§1t4417s0§ < 100) this.§1t4417s0§ = 100;` (:3117-3120). The DAMAGE switch at :3259-3271 is the exact inverse: Light damage scales, Balanced damage scales with the same coefficient as its reach, Heavy damage is a flat *1.4 (:3270). So Light trades fixed long reach for scaling damage and Heavy trades fixed high damage for scaling reach - and Heavy's reach can never fall below 100 units. Two consequences for the ledger: 'Heavy's reach also scales x0.5->x0.9' has the wrong low endpoint (m=1 gives 0.54, and the 100 floor may bind first), and the quoted reach triple 300/200/100 cannot be a mastery-ceiling row off one base, because the ceiling multipliers are 1.4 / 1.20 / 0.90, which is not 3:2:1.
new_findings.ledger_text: A level-1 Shugyosha does Light x0.5 / Balanced x1.0 / Heavy x1.4 (Heavy is fixed); Heavy's *reach* also scales x0.5->x0.9.
new_findings.lane_impact: L5 combat-core: reach is a per-stance function of BASE_SLASH_LENGTH, not a literal px triple - Light 1.4 flat, Balanced 1+0.02m, Heavy max(0.5+0.04m, floor 100). Combat-core blocker (1) 'reach cap in stage px per stance' becomes 'measure ONE base slash length', not three.

new_findings.text: The packet stops at two of the third bar's three states. §1t113s0§.as:348-359 is the third: at ratio >= 1 the same TextField takes §1t5203s0§ = `"<font color='#000000'>" + getString(175) + "</font>"` (built at :110), i.e. BLACK 'Critical Hit', and :350-352 fire `§1t88s0§.instance.§1t1516s0§("Snd_criticalDamage")` on the transition into that state - guarded so it plays once, not per frame. So the single track under HP and Chi is a three-state readout on one 0..192 resource: empty -> #BBBBBB getString(960); filling -> no text; full -> #000000 getString(175) plus a one-shot sound. Under correction C3 the audio is recovered, so Snd_criticalDamage is a nameable, shippable stem rather than a TODO.

new_findings.text: The packet notes that string 960 is unresolvable from the android table but not why, and the mechanism is a genuine, first-hand v0.717-vs-v0.682 divergence - one of the very few that discharges part of the C2 caveat instead of restating it. Android BattleUI.as:262 is the ENTIRE reload-bar text logic: `this.crittext.visible = percentage >= 1 && this.reloadbar.visible;` - the android build shows the crit text at full and nothing at all otherwise. It has no empty-state label on the bar. Instead its 'Change Stance' string lives on a mouse rollover over the portrait: :192-193 add MOUSE_OVER/MOUSE_OUT listeners on battlemodebust bound to showChangeStanceLabel/hideChangeStanceLabel (:430-440), which toggle changestancelabel and the bust highlight together. The web build replaced that hover affordance with a persistent on-bar notice, which is why getString(960) exists in v0.717 and is missing from the v0.682 table (strings.json["960"] returns None). Android also normalises the ratio itself before the call, while the web computes (reload-48)/(max-48) inside §1t5205s0§.
new_findings.lane_impact: L8 ui-hud: build the WEB behaviour (persistent on-bar empty-state label), not the android hover tooltip - and record this as a discharged C2 instance: the two builds' battle HUDs are NOT at parity on this element.

new_findings.text: Correcting the packet's own lane_impact, which says the HUD 'needs a Change Stance button next to the portrait'. It is not next to the portrait; it IS the portrait. Android BattleUI.as:275-277 reads `if(this.battlemodebust.hitTestPoint(mousex,mousey)) { this.stanceButtonClick(); }`, and :112-113 set `battlemodebust.highlight.visible = false; battlemodebust.buttonMode = true;`. The web twin is identical in shape: §1t113s0§.as:148-149 set `§1t5158s0§.highlight.visible = false; §1t5158s0§.buttonMode = true;` and :379-381 hit-test §1t5158s0§ into §1t5207s0§. So §1t5158s0§ = battlemodebust. The stance COLOUR rides the same object: web §1t5208s0§ (:482-485) does `§1t5158s0§.§1t15895s0§.gotoAndStop(param1)` against android setStanceColor (:372-375) `battlemodebust.stancecolor1.gotoAndStop(num)`, called from the stance switch with 1=Light, 2=Balanced, 3=Heavy (§1t99s0§.as:3101, :3112, :3127). That means the stance-coloured portrait ring the ledger already records as item 10 and the stance button are ONE widget, and the ring index is an explicit 1/2/3 frame number rather than an inferred palette.
